content.comment_body: I am working with [product_name] and [product_name] using [product_name] version [version_no]. I attempted to connect them, but there is no response, and data is not being received. Communication is not functioning.
It appears there is a general communication issue between [product_name] and [product_name]. First, have you ensured that the put/get option is enabled in the configuration?

Yes, I did enable that option, but it did not help. When I try sending a pulse from [product_name] to [product_name] with firmware [version_no], neither device is sending or receiving anything. Adding a MOVE block appears to disable the output ENO.

Both devices are on the same network: 192.168.0.1, with a router. [product_name] firmware [version_no] has IP 192.168.0.20. [product_name] with [product_name] software [version_no] has IP 192.168.0.15. TSAP settings: 20,00 and 10,01.
I tried the same experiment and faced the same issue. I'm using [product_name] and [product_name] with version [version_no]. We need a solution for this.
A new question published by [user_name] was moved to a separate thread regarding data writing from [product_name] to [product_name] not working. Best regards [user_name]

Set up the connection with [product_name] as client and [product_name] as server. In the engineering software, remove the check mark for ''Active connection establishment'' in the special connection properties. In protection and security settings, ensure ''permanent access for PUT/GET communication from remote partner'' is checked.

I am experiencing similar issues. Although I managed to establish communication between [product_name] and [product_name] for one sensor, the addressing in PUT/GET and how addresses are mapped in each device is unclear to me. I am still testing many settings and haven't found a reliable solution yet.
No solution received for you in a private message? For me, it works as I described previously. I can send my test project if you are interested.

The private message contained basic settings only. I may not fully understand the addressing part, which is causing issues in my testing. Communication between the devices works, but the address usage in [product_name] and [product_name] is more complex than expected.
In another topic, I will provide you with an answer and an example matching your requirements, publicly on the forum.

Hello, In [product_name], all addressing uses DB1.BDXzzz, where zzz is the memory address. Active connection establishment is enabled. Read and write both work. If a write connection error occurs and the red backlight is on, changing the TSAP helped me. The TSAP can be changed by adding a new connection; this increments the TSAP and older connections may be deleted.
If [product_name] is configured as client and [product_name] as server, you don't need to use DB1. You can address the server's operands directly from the client's connection list.

Despite activating relevant settings such as PUT/GET communication, expected data exchange still does not occur.
